What a /20 means

A /20 holds 4,096 addresses. Blocks this size are usually site or data-centre allocations that get divided into smaller subnets.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /20 uses 20 network bits and leaves 12 host bits, so the block contains 4,096 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−20) − 2 = 4,096 − 2 = 4,094.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.240.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.15.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/20

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/20 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /20?

4,094. A /20 has 4,096 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 4,094 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /20?

255.255.240.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.15.255.
